AttachmentResponse.description: EDR-aligned attachment metadata. The base64 `content` is never returned.

disposition.description: MIME disposition (e.g. `attachment` or `inline`). Runtime passes through the stored value without enforcing an enum.

sha256.description: SHA-256 hex digest of the attachment content.

url.description: Telnyx-hosted public URL for the attachment content.

CreateEmailInboxRequest.description: Both fields are optional. Omitting `username` generates one; omitting `domain_id` uses the account's shared inbound subdomain. Omitting both creates an instant inbox with a generated username.

domain_id.description: Account-owned, inbound-enabled domain UUID. The account's shared inbound subdomain is allocated when omitted.

username.description: Inbox local part. Trimmed and lowercased before validation; the normalized value must be 1-64 characters, start and end with a letter or digit, and contain only letters, digits, dots, hyphens, and underscores. Generated when omitted.

DailySendLimitError.description: Error envelope returned when the account's daily recipient quota is exhausted before message creation.

detail.example: Daily send limit of 1000 recipients exceeded. The limit resets at midnight UTC.

DomainGraduationLimitExceededError.description: Error envelope returned when a newly sending custom domain on shared egress would exceed its current daily graduation ceiling. The send is rejected before message creation.

detail.example: Daily send limit of 250 recipients for this sender domain exceeded. The limit resets at midnight UTC.

meta.description: Bounded retry guidance. Each field is omitted when unknown.

remaining_today.description: Recipient headroom remaining for the sender-domain identity before this rejected request.

retry_after_seconds.description: Seconds until the next UTC-midnight reset.

EmailEventType.description: Bare stored event names returned by message history. In addition to the normal send and delivery lifecycle, polling can expose suppression, scan, and quarantine lifecycle rows. Sharp canonical names gw_reject, injection_timeout, and expired distinguish gateway rejection, ambiguous injection timeout, and MTA expiration. The failed and bounced names remain valid for system/admin failures and hard bounces respectively. Existing stored rows retain their original names.

domain.description: Domain name used by the inbox address.

page_cursor.description: Cursor for the next inbox page, when more results are available.

inline_css.description: Present when true in the immediate create response. Not persisted; absent on subsequent GET requests.

metadata.description: Customer-supplied metadata stored with the message.

recipient_statuses.description:
Per-status recipient counts for the message. Present only for outbound messages
with recipient rows. Keys are recipient statuses, values are counts.
Example: `{"delivered": 998, "bounced": 2}`.

sandbox.description: Present when sandbox mode was used.

scheduled_at.description: Present when a scheduled_at value was stored. Persists even after the scheduled send has been processed or cancelled.

suppressed.description: Recipients excluded from delivery by suppression checks, with reasons. On batch items, present when that item had suppressed recipients; all other recipients of the item still receive the message. For single sends this information appears at the top level of the response instead (see EmailMessageResponse.suppressed).

tags.description: Customer-supplied tags stored with the message.

suppressed.description: Recipients removed by suppression checks when at least one recipient remains and the message is accepted.

EmailMessageStatus.description: Current status of an email message. Lifecycle statuses (queued, scheduled, etc.) are set on creation. Delivery statuses (delivered, bounced, etc.) are updated by delivery event consumers.

EmbeddedMessageEvent.description: An event embedded in a message response. The dedicated per-message events endpoint additionally returns event_type and canonical_event_type.

code.description: Telnyx error code. Send admission errors include account daily quota 10011 and sender-domain ramp code domain_graduation_limit_exceeded. Edge idempotency errors use 10027 or 10036. Fallback 404/500 responses from the framework may use string status codes ('404', '500') instead.

detail.description: Human-readable error detail. Changeset responses may return a structured object.

meta.description: Additional metadata. Present on 401 errors with a documentation URL.

html.description: Optional HTML note prepended to the generated forwarded-message block. Blank values are treated as omitted.

text.description: Optional plain-text note prepended to the generated forwarded-message block. Blank values are treated as omitted.

labels.description: Mutable thread labels used for agent workflow state. Independent of the labels on the thread's messages, and distinct from the send-time `tags` on outbound messages.

message_count.description: Total inbound and outbound messages in the thread.

unread_count.description: Unread inbound messages; outbound messages never increment this count.

InboxActionEmailAddressInput.description: Email address accepted by inbox message actions, as a string or an object with `email` and optional `name`.

InboxActionRecipientInput.description: One recipient or a recipient array. Each recipient may be an email string or an object with `email` and optional `name`.

InboxFilterEntry.description:
An exact sender address (`user@example.com`) or domain wildcard
(`@example.com`). Values are trimmed and normalized to lowercase.

LabelMutationRequest.description: Labels to add or remove. Both operations are idempotent set operations, so a retried request converges instead of failing.

labels.description: One or more labels. Each label is a freeform, case-sensitive string of at most 255 characters; a message or thread may carry at most 50 labels. The `telnyx:` prefix is a reserved system namespace and is rejected on customer writes.

ReplaceInboxFiltersRequest.description:
The complete filter configuration. An omitted list is replaced with an
empty list. Unknown keys are ignored by the controller.

ReplyEmailInboxMessageRequest.description: At least one of `text` or `html` must contain a non-whitespace body. Recipients are derived from the source message; caller-supplied `to`, `cc`, or `bcc` values are ignored.

ReputationSuspendedError.description: Non-standard error envelope returned when the sending domain's reputation band is 'poor'. Uses string code `reputation_suspended` instead of a numeric code.

RequiredInboxActionRecipientInput.description: One recipient or a non-empty recipient array. Each recipient may be an email string or an object with `email` and optional `name`.

override_allowed.description: Whether an authorized send may override this suppression.

reason.description: Suppression reason returned by the recipient suppression service.

scope.description: Scope at which the suppression applies.

has_quoted_text.description: Whether conservative plain-text extraction detected a quoted tail. False does not prove that the source contains no quoted content.

html_body_url.description: URL for an offloaded HTML body. Null means the body is not offloaded to a URL; an inline HTML body may still exist but is not returned on list reads. Reply extraction uses only the plain-text body during ingest.

labels.description: Mutable message labels used for agent workflow state (for example `spam`, `needs_review`, `processed`). Distinct from the immutable send-time `tags` on outbound messages: labels are never propagated to Email Detail Records or Mission Control reporting. Always empty for outbound messages. Labels on a message are independent of the labels on its thread.

message_id.description: RFC Message-ID header. Null is possible for legacy outbound messages.

read_at.description: Time the inbound message was marked read. Null means unread.

received_at.description: Receipt time for inbound messages; null for outbound messages.

references.description: Ordered RFC Message-ID values from the References header.

reply_text.description: Conservatively extracted new-reply content persisted from the plain-text body during ingest. Null means no plain-text extraction input was available or extraction was skipped or failed; HTML bodies are not parsed.

sent_at.description: Creation/send-acceptance time for outbound messages; null for inbound messages.

status.description: Received for inbound messages; the current send status for outbound messages.

text_body_url.description: URL for an offloaded plain-text body. Null means the body is not offloaded to a URL; an inline plain-text body may still exist but is not returned on list reads. `reply_text` and `has_quoted_text` are persisted during ingest before any body offload.

read_at.description: Set to `true` for server time, an ISO 8601 timestamp for an explicit read time, or `null` to mark unread.

suppressed.description: Present when every recipient is suppressed, so the request is rejected and no message is created.

page_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page, when more results are available.

BearerAuth.description: Telnyx API key supplied as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. In production, auth may be validated by the API gateway and forwarded via Telnyx auth headers.

Payment.description: Machine Payment Protocol credential used on paid retries, sent as `Authorization: Payment ...`. Obtained by paying a challenge returned in the `WWW-Authenticate` header of a 402 response. This is not a Telnyx API key; initial challenge requests use standard bearer authentication instead.

Sends from the inbox address through the standard email send pipeline to caller-supplied
To, Cc, and Bcc recipients. `to` must contain at least one recipient. Optional `text` and
`html` are prepended to a forwarded-message block containing the original metadata and
available body content. The subject is prefixed with `Fwd:` unless it already has that prefix.

Threading headers are derived from the original message: `In-Reply-To` is set to its
RFC Message-ID, and `References` contains the original References values plus that
Message-ID, de-duplicated and limited to the most recent 20 values.

delete.description:
Removes one or more labels from a message. Idempotent — removing a
label the message does not carry is a no-op and still returns 200.
Removal is case-sensitive.
delete.summary: Remove labels from an inbox message

post.description:
Adds one or more mutable labels to a message. Labels carry agent
workflow state such as `spam`, `needs_review`, or `processed`.

Labels are **not** the same as the send-time `tags` on outbound
messages: `tags` are immutable and propagate to Email Detail Records
and Mission Control for billing attribution, while labels are mailbox
state that never reaches the reporting contract.

The operation is an idempotent set union — adding a label the message
already carries is a no-op and still returns 200. Labels are
case-sensitive, and message labels are independent of thread labels.
post.summary: Add labels to an inbox message
